title: NorthernLight Systems — Partner integration kickoff
summary: Introductory partner discovery between Redwood and NorthernLight Systems focused on integration patterns for private/hybrid GPU deployments, validation of latency targets for real-time features, and enterprise security/compliance needs. Customer is evaluating on-prem plus VPC-first models; timeline is end-of-Q1 pilot with procurement and legal loop following security artifacts. Agreed next step: Redwood to run a short on-prem/H100 benchmark and share partner integration guide + security pack.
topics: integration patterns (hosted vs dedicated vs private)
GPU options and perf (A100 vs H100)
commercial model and partner GTM motion
transcript:
Meeting Header: Date: 2027-11-02 14:30 UTC | Duration: 54m | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jared (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood SE), Rohit (CTO), Elena (Partnerships), Samir (Infra), Tina (Procurement)

[00:00] Maya Chen: hi everyone, thanks for joining, i'm maya from Redwood, i'm the account lead, with me is jared and priya on the systems team. quick round of intros?
[00:14] Rohit Malhotra: hey all, roh it, CTO at NorthernLight systems, we're looking at inference partners for our next-gen search and summarization features.
[00:24] Elena García: elena here, partnerships and integrations, we'll be owning the partner side.
[00:30] Samir Khan: samir, infra lead. we've got hybrid infra today, mostly GCP and some on-prem colo.
[00:38] Tina Le: tina from procurement, i'll loop in on commercial terms later.
[00:42] Jared Patel: great, thanks. quick agenda — integration options, perf targets, security requirements, and an initial pilot scope.
[00:52] Maya Chen: and any must-haves up front? timeline?
[00:55] Rohit Malhotra: timeline is Q1 pilot; procurement wants vendor security package before we start pilots. success metrics: p99 latency under 150ms for single-turn chat at 2k context and cost per 1k tokens under our target, roughly $0.35.
[01:20] Priya Rao: okay good to know, we'll capture that. quick question on where you'll want to run — do you prefer VPC-hosted Redwood or fully on-prem?
[01:30] Samir Khan: VPC-first with option to air-gap some sensitive workloads on-prem. so we need private deployment path and KMS integration for keys.
[01:42] Maya Chen: we support VPC/private control plane and an on-prem package. we integrate with customer KMS/HSM — some customers use cloud KMS, others use on-prem HSMs. any compliance concerns?
[01:54] Elena García: SOC 2 is baseline, and we'll need audit logs for all calls and redaction controls. also SSO with SAML, RBAC tenants for dev vs prod teams.
[02:08] Jared Patel: all standard — we can provide the security pack and audit log samples. small note: our KV cache is often helpful for prefix caching, that reduces token costs — sometimes transcribed as K V cache in notes.
[02:23] Rohit Malhotra: yes, caching sounds useful. concerning perf — what's realistic for H100 vs A100 on 8k contexts? we saw different numbers in public benchmarks.
[02:35] Priya Rao: H100 will give you stronger throughput and usually lower p99s for long contexts; A100 can be tuned with quantization, but there are tradeoffs on quality. we should run a workload-specific benchmark for your prompts.
[02:52] Samir Khan: what's involved in the benchmark? can you run in our colo?
[02:58] Jared Patel: we can do two paths: 1) Redwood runs a head-to-head on our lab H100 and A100 images using a sampled prompt set you provide; 2) if you prefer, we can install a partner agent in your colo under NDA and run in-situ tests. the first is faster; the second gives most realistic network latencies.
[03:20] Rohit Malhotra: timeline wise, we want test results before procurement engages final terms — so within two weeks ideally.
[03:27] Maya Chen: two weeks is tight but doable for the lab test. for in-situ, it's usually 3–4 weeks with procurement and network whitelisting.
[03:37] Tina Le: procurement note: we'll need contract templates and a partner SLA. also, any references or case studies?
[03:46] Maya Chen: we'll include an enterprise reference list; also partner integration guide and security artifacts. link: https://redwood.com/partner-guide (note: internal doc link).
[03:59] Elena García: in terms of integration patterns, we need clarity on model routing — can you route between lower-cost quantized variants and full-precision ones based on latency windows?
[04:12] Priya Rao: yes, smart routing is supported — policies can route by latency requirement, cost tier, or region. we also support automatic fallback to compatible variants if a primary model is out of capacity.
[04:26] Rohit Malhotra: excellent — we run peak traffic at end-of-day and need graceful degradation not to fail hard.
[04:33] Jared Patel: we'll also surface tracing for requests in the console so your SREs can pinpoint regressions.
[04:41] Samir Khan: network: will you support private peering to our VPC or need a VPN?
[04:48] Maya Chen: both options. private peering (direct connect) preferred for sustained throughput; VPN can be used for pilot/POC. for on-prem air-gapped we'll provide an on-prem package with outbound-only control plane if needed.
[05:03] Rohit Malhotra: are there any open-source bits we need to run?
[05:07] Priya Rao: the on-prem agent is a lightweight package that bundles runtime and orchestration shims; no heavy ops changes, but we'll work with your infra team on kernel versions and GPU drivers.
[05:18] Samir Khan: driver/compatibility — we run mixed driver stack at the colo, need to ensure runtime supports our kernel.
[05:25] Jared Patel: we'll collect your host profile; our runtime supports standard NVIDIA drivers for A100/H100; if you have older stacks we'll validate during tech onboarding.
[05:36] Rohit Malhotra: any unexpected costs we should watch for? eg network egress or cache storage?
[05:41] Maya Chen: main units are per-token inference and dedicated capacity for reserved pools. additional items are long retention for logs and extra observability retention. network egress is typically charged by hosting cloud if using hosted model; for private/on-prem that's internal.
[05:58] Elena García: GTM question — how do partners typically co-sell? we want clarity on reseller motions and lead routing.
[06:06] Maya Chen: we have a partner program with co-selling playbooks; exec sponsor alignment and an MDR for joint proof points helps. we'll send the partner GTM deck.
[06:16] Tina Le: legal will need the data processing addendum and security questionnaire.
[06:20] Maya Chen: we'll attach the security packet and an example DPA.
[06:25] Rohit Malhotra: ok to recap, we need: lab perf run on H100/A100 with our prompt set (by 2027-11-10), security pack + DPA, partner GTM deck, and a pilot scope doc.
[06:37] Maya Chen: yes, and we'll propose a pilot SOW. any blockers on your side?
[06:42] Samir Khan: network approval and getting us a sample prompt set is the main blocker. we'll share a 200-query bundle.
[06:50] Priya Rao: perfect, once we have the prompts we'll schedule benchmark runs and share results with latency/cost breakdown.
[06:58] Maya Chen: thanks all, i'll follow up with meeting notes and next steps.
[07:03] Elena García: thanks everyone, appreciate the clarity.
[07:06] Tina Le: thanks.
[07:08] Rohit Malhotra: thanks, bye.

End of transcript. Note: occasional word errors in auto-transcribe (e.g., 'K V cache' for KV cache, 'V P C' for VPC, some names slightly off), verified post-call by AE.
next_steps: Redwood to run lab benchmark (H100 vs A100) with customer's 200-query prompt set — target 2027-11-10
Share security pack, DPA template, and partner GTM deck — Redwood to send by 2027-11-04
Schedule technical onboarding call for in-situ pilot if customer chooses on-prem — tentative week of 2027-11-15

Maya Chen (Redwood AE) | send security pack, DPA sample, partner GTM deck, and partner integration guide link | 2027-11-04
